claim_text: The USFS Wildfire Risk to Communities conditional risk to potential structures applies, per FSim flame-length class FLP1 to FLP6, a structure loss of 25/40/55/70/85/100 (tree), 20/35/50/65/80/95 (shrub) and 10/25/40/55/70/85 (grass/herbaceous), where 0 is no damage and 100 is complete loss.
permitted_inference: Use the shrub values for the house (WRC_RESPONSE_FUNCTION_TABLE).
reasoning: Published, national, on Hazard's own axis.
update_trigger: A revised WRC edition changes the response.

claim_text: The response represents 'the relative effect of wildfire on structures (i.e., relative degree of damage or loss)' and cRPS is 'essentially conditional Net Value Change' for a house; WRC uses it as a 0-100 index to rank places.
permitted_inference: Read the value as the expected share of the structure lost, given fire at the location.
prohibited_inference: Present the reading as the source's own repair-cost statement.
reasoning: The source says degree of damage or loss of a structure on a 0 (none) to 100 (complete) scale; reading it as repair cost over replacement cost new is this cell's step (WFRE-C004).

claim_text: The three response functions 'reflect the assumption that consequence is greatest in tree fuels, lower in shrubs, and lowest in grass fuels'; the record gives no derivation, elicitation or field calibration for the numbers.
permitted_inference: Carry the values as agency judgment, checked against DINS (WFRE-C008) and NRI (WFRE-C013).
prohibited_inference: Treat the lifeform ordering or the 15-point steps as measured.
reasoning: Stated as an assumption in the source.
update_trigger: A published derivation or field test of the response.

claim_text: Reading the WRC loss value as repair cost / structure replacement cost new of the same building.
permitted_inference: Use the value directly as the failure-unit damage ratio.
prohibited_inference: Add contents or land to the same ratio.
reasoning: A house reported as complete loss is rebuilt, so 100 = full replacement cost new is the natural reading; partial values have no stated cost basis.
update_trigger: A cost-based statement from the source.

claim_text: FSim flame-length classes are FLP1 < 2 ft, FLP2 2-<4, FLP3 4-<6, FLP4 6-<8, FLP5 8-<12, FLP6 12+ ft, conditional on a fire; WRC's FLEP4 and FLEP8 are sums of its FLP classes above 4 and 8 ft, so WRC uses the same class boundaries (at 30 m, WildEST) as Hazard's 270 m FSim product.
permitted_inference: Apply the WRC class responses to Hazard's class states 1 to 6.
prohibited_inference: Claim the 30 m WRC and 270 m FSim class mixes are the same at a place.
reasoning: Same class scheme; different resolution and fuel vintage (WRC fuels end of 2022, Hazard's FSim LANDFIRE 2020).

claim_text: Hazard delivers, per 0.25-degree cell, an annual burn probability on burnable pixels (lambda = -ln(1-BP)) and the conditional FLP1-6 mix; it looks up damage at the exact class state (0 = no event), rejects fractional states and a burn probability in the damage call, and couples with p_hit = 1.
permitted_inference: Accept exact integer states 0 to 6 only.
prohibited_inference: Accept a flame length in feet, a burn probability or a fractional state as the damage input.

claim_text: Hazard does not deliver the fuel lifeform (tree, shrub, grass) that the WRC response depends on.
permitted_inference: Use the middle (shrub) response for every cell; carry tree and grass as sensitivity (D-WFRE-05).
prohibited_inference: Pick a lifeform per cell without a Hazard input.
reasoning: JL decided shrub as the default (2026-10-18).
update_trigger: Hazard adds a lifeform per cell (e.g. from LANDFIRE EVT).

claim_text: Among 12,188 inspected one-storey wood/vinyl/combustible-sided asphalt-roof houses in DINS (2013-2025), 58.7% were destroyed and 36.5% undamaged; of those damaged, 92.4% were destroyed. Mean damage (band midpoints, destroyed = 100%) is 0.59 over all fires, 0.29 in fires recording at least 20% no-damage, 0.33 without the Camp Fire, 0.65 without the 2025 Los Angeles fires.
parameter_or_rule: house level check; near all-or-nothing outcome
permitted_inference: Treat the USFS response (grid-average house loss about 0.5 given fire) as consistent in level with observed house loss given exposure.
prohibited_inference: Calibrate the response to DINS (no flame length is recorded).
reasoning: DINS covers structures in or near perimeters; no-damage records are incomplete in many fires.
update_trigger: A DINS record with local fire intensity.

claim_text: Within the same fires, metal-wall metal-roof commercial buildings lost 0.79 times as much as those houses (258 buildings, 38 fires; 90% range 0.61-0.99) and multi-storey stucco/brick/cement commercial buildings 0.93 times (204 buildings, 17 fires; 0.66-1.38). Pooled over all fires the ratios are 0.30 and 0.42, and 0.27-0.60 and 0.28-0.81 across subsets.
permitted_inference: Use 0.8 (warehouse) and 0.9 (office) on the house curve (D-WFRE-07).
prohibited_inference: Use the pooled ratio as the building effect (it mixes which fires hit which buildings).
reasoning: Comparing inside the same fire holds the fire, weather and suppression fixed.
update_trigger: A loss study of large sprinklered warehouses or offices in wildfires.

claim_text: DINS commercial groups are California commercial buildings of any size and use; the reference warehouse (100,000 ft2, sprinklered) and office (54,000 ft2, sprinklered) are larger and DINS records no sprinkler or size field.
permitted_inference: Label the factors a T4 transfer with the 0.3-1.0 range in sensitivity.
prohibited_inference: Claim the factors are measured for the reference buildings.
reasoning: Size, sprinklers and fire-department access could make the reference buildings do better; water supply often fails in large wildland-urban fires.

claim_text: In DINS 2013-2018, building features that block ember entry (enclosed eaves, vent screens, multi-pane windows) explained more of survival than defensible space; any single variable explained little; many 'fire-safe' structures were destroyed.
parameter_or_rule: why flame length is a weak predictor
permitted_inference: State that the flame-length class carries limited information about a building's loss; keep the curve a screening average.
reasoning: Embers and building-to-building spread act beyond the flame front.

claim_text: The house profile has a vented attic with no ember-resistant vent rating, vinyl siding and asphalt shingles; it declares no vegetation buffer or neighbouring buildings. These match the DINS house group and carry no mitigation credit.
permitted_inference: Bind the WRC home response to the house without adjustment.
prohibited_inference: Credit defensible space or ember-resistant vents.

claim_text: On Hazard's grid the curves give yearly building loss 2.0x (house), 1.6x (warehouse) and 1.8x (office) NRI nationally (median cell 3.0x, 2.4x, 2.7x), rank correlation 0.88; the West is at 1.75x and the East at 4.7x (median cell, house).
permitted_inference: Report the ratio; flag Hazard-side causes.
reasoning: NRI is a county average of reported losses for all buildings.
